# Present-corner section control with the actual triangle scale

This note combines two exact inputs for possible ordinary-to-mixed
section-weight transfer. It proves the displayed necessary inequalities;
Sections 5--6 subsequently complete that transfer for present corners
in a specified small-A, bad-source triangle regime, and give its scoped
endpoint-gap descent consequence. This is not a general OC theorem.

## 1. A far residual corner controls its original section

Let A and B be planar convex bodies. Let nonzero spanning normals
v_1,v_2,v_3 sum to zero, and fix a point y. Put

    h_i=h_B(v_i)-v_i.y,      W=sum_i h_i=sum_i h_B(v_i)>0,
    H_i^A={x:v_i.(x-y)>=-h_i},
    U_i=|A intersect H_i^A|,  a=|A|,
    sigma_Ai=H_1(A intersect {v_i.(x-y)=-h_i})/||v_i||.

Assume the indicated i-th A cut is proper, meaning its line meets
the interior of A. Assume also that the actual residual corner

    R_i=A intersect intersection_(j!=i){v_j.(x-y)<-h_j}

is nonempty. It then has positive area: take any of its points and a
nearby interior point of A along a segment to a fixed interior point;
the strict inequalities persist in a small open neighborhood.

Define the actual shifted tail and its elementary lower bound by

    T_i=|A intersect {v_i.(x-y)>=W-h_i}|,
    delta_i=max(0,a-U_j-U_k).

**Lemma 1.** One has 0<T_i<U_i and T_i>=delta_i. Moreover

    sigma_Ai <= (2/W)(U_i-sqrt(U_i T_i))
              <= (2/W)(U_i-sqrt(U_i delta_i)).             (1)

In particular sigma_Ai<2U_i/W. The hypothesis that R_i is actually
present cannot be dropped when delta_i=0.

**Proof.** The normals sum to zero. Every point missing the other two
A caps satisfies v_i.(x-y)>h_j+h_k=W-h_i. Thus R_i lies in the strict
shifted tail and T_i>=|R_i|>=a-U_j-U_k. The positivity of R_i gives
T_i>0. Also W>0 because an interior point of B has strictly smaller
values than all three supporting values; summing those strict gaps
gives W>0.

Put F(t)=|A intersect {v_i.(x-y)>=-h_i+t}|. It is positive on
[0,W]. Its square root is concave there: convexity of A gives
Minkowski containment of interpolated caps, and planar Brunn-Minkowski
then gives the root concavity. The original proper cut has a continuous
section length in an open interval of thresholds. Coarea therefore
gives F'(0)=-sigma_Ai and

    (sqrt F)'(0)=-sigma_Ai/(2sqrt(U_i)).

The tangent inequality for this concave function at zero, evaluated
at W, reads

    sqrt(T_i)<=sqrt(U_i)-W sigma_Ai/(2sqrt(U_i)).

Rearranging proves the first inequality in (1). The second follows
from T_i>=delta_i. The original proper cut and the positive shifted
tail ensure a positive-area slab between the two levels, so T_i<U_i.
Finally T_i>0 makes the bound sigma_Ai<2U_i/W strict. QED.

If an independently proved sharper lower bound for the SAME actual
tail T_i is available, it may replace delta_i in (1). For example the
shifted-cover bound for the largest A cap in
`candidate 6b20e938071f0379`
uses delta_*=a-U_mid-U_min/4 under that note's additional bad-source
and nonheavy assumptions. No such stronger bound is assumed here.

## 2. Exact area of the actual triangle in signed-row variables

Let K be a triangle with source y and the same balanced normals.
Assume the three middle caps each isolate one distinct strict vertex,
with no other vertex on a cutting line. Use the normalized positive
heights a_i and row differences d_i from
`candidate 919c51f1d263878e`.
To avoid confusing normalized heights with the area a above, define
the unnormalized total height explicitly as

    H=sum_i v_i.(P_i-y)>0,
    D=|det(v_1,v_2)|>0,
    k=|K|,
    f_i=2a_i/sqrt(q_i),

where q_i is the i-th middle cap fraction. Put

    R=1+(sum_i d_i)^2-2sum_i d_i^2.

**Lemma 2.** The exact, actual scale identity is

    R=4-sum_i f_i^2=8Dk/H^2>0.                            (2)

**Proof.** Map x to (v_1.(x-y),v_2.(x-y)) and divide by H. The
resulting triangle has area Dk/H^2 and vertices given by the first
two rows of the normalized balanced matrix with diagonal a_i and
off-diagonal entries -b_ij. The sum of its three consecutive origin
determinants is

    sum_(i<j)(a_i a_j-b_ij b_ji).

All three determinants are positive because y is interior. Substitute

    g_i=1-d_(i+1)+d_(i+2),
    s_i=g_i-2a_i,
    b_i,i+1=(s_i+d_i)/2,
    b_i,i+2=(s_i-d_i)/2,
    sum_i a_i=1.

Expanding and cancelling the a_i terms gives

    sum_(i<j)(a_i a_j-b_ij b_ji)
        =[1+(sum_i d_i)^2-2sum_i d_i^2]/4.

The triangle area is half that determinant sum, proving the last
equality in (2). Also f_i^2=g_i^2-d_i^2 and
sum_i g_i^2=3+3sum_i d_i^2-(sum_i d_i)^2. Subtracting sum d_i^2
gives sum f_i^2=3+2sum d_i^2-(sum d_i)^2=4-R. QED.

Under the cap ceiling q_i<=128/279, the Lorentz moment gives
F:=sum f_i>=2/sqrt(128/279)>59/20. Summing the three Lorentz
inequalities gives sum f_i^2<=24-4F-F^2. Therefore the useful
explicit lower scale bound is

    R>=F^2+4F-20>201/400.                                 (3)

This is a bound on the shape factor of the actual triangle. The
quantity H has not been freely normalized independently of B.

## 3. Keeping the support triangle of the same B

The support triangle

    T_B={x:v_i.(x-y)<=h_i for i=1,2,3}

contains the actual B. Its area is W^2/(2D). Indeed the same two-normal
coordinate map has determinant D; the three inequalities form a
canonical right triangle with leg lengths W, possibly translated.
Thus, writing b=|B| and beta=b/k>0, (2) gives

    b<=W^2/(2D),
    H/W<=2/sqrt(beta R).                                  (4)

The i-th middle section has normalized length

    sigma_Ki=2k q_i/(H a_i)
            =4k sqrt(q_i)/(H f_i).                       (5)

Combining (1), (4), and (5), for every actually present R_i,

    sigma_Ai/sigma_Ki
      <= f_i (U_i/k)[1-sqrt(delta_i/U_i)]
                      /[sqrt(q_i) sqrt(beta R)].          (6)

Every scale in this inequality belongs to the same bodies, normals,
and source. The only relaxation of B is its actual support-triangle
containment. Replacing delta_i by a sharper certified lower tail bound
preserves (6).

In the exact three-fiber common-budget setting, write alpha=a/k and
r=Q/k. If U_i+k q_i=Q, then

    U_i/k=r-q_i,
    delta_i/k=max(0,alpha-(r-q_j)-(r-q_k)).                 (7)

These substitutions preserve the correlation between the three
actual cap masses. They do not posit independent endpoint cap menus.

## 4. What a mixed-weight transfer would still require

Let lambda_i be the ordinary inverse-middle-section weights and put
u_i=sigma_Ai/sigma_Ki. The mixed section weights are

    p_i=[lambda_i/(1+2u_i)]/sum_j[lambda_j/(1+2u_j)].

Since all u_j>=0,

    p_i>=lambda_i/[1+2u_i(1-lambda_i)].                   (8)

For an ordinary triangle satisfying the cap/profile theorem,
lambda_i>223/1000. Consequently a sufficient condition for p_i>=2/9
is u_i<=7/3108. Area alone, or the two-chord area products alone,
does not imply this small individual ratio: a thin actual A may have
one long proper section. The earlier exact collapsing-triangle source
already certifies that limitation.

Equations (6)--(7) supply additional actual corner mass and compatible
scale information. The next section uses these correlations to prove
a transfer under explicit bad-source and small-area hypotheses. A
corner absent from A must still be handled by its separate multiplicity
argument; (6) may not be applied to it merely by setting delta_i=0.

## 5. Present singleton corners have mixed weight greater than 2/9

**Theorem 3.** Let A,K,B be planar convex bodies with (A+B)/2 contained
in K, where K is a triangle. Let y belong to int K and let nonzero
spanning normals v_1+v_2+v_3=0 be given. Use the three ambient caps

    v_i.(x-y)+(v_i.y-h_B(v_i))z>=0

at the three integer levels -1,0,1. Assume all their A cuts are proper
and their captured areas have the same total Q:

    U_i+k q_i=Q.

Write a=|A|, k=|K|, b=|B| and assume

    Q<=2(a+k+b)/9,       b<=a+k,       a<b/32.              (9)

Then, for every actually present residual corner R_i, the mixed
section weight

    p_i=[1/(sigma_Ki+2sigma_Ai)]
                    /sum_j[1/(sigma_Kj+2sigma_Aj)]

is strictly greater than 2/9. No separate assumption on a sorted
ordinary K cap profile is required. The theorem itself does not
require the displayed caps to attain the depth; genuine criticality
is required for the shell-descent corollary below.

**Proof.** Put alpha=a/k, beta=b/k, r=Q/k and u_i=U_i/k. To avoid a
conflict with the determinant D above, denote the cap-sum slack by

    Delta=125/93-sum_i q_i.

The three A halfplanes cover the plane because their thresholds sum
to -W<0. Thus E=sum_i U_i-a>=0. The three middle halfplanes also cover
the plane. One of them contains the ordinary centroid of K, so the
ordinary planar Grunbaum inequality gives Q>=4k/9. Combining this
with (9) yields k<=a+b.

The nonheavy condition for B and a<b/32 imply

    alpha<1/31,      beta>30/31,
    r<=4(1+alpha)/9<128/279=:c,
    q_i<=r<c.                                            (10)

The audited sharp triangle incidence theorem therefore applies: each
middle cap isolates one distinct strict vertex. The Lorentz variables
f_i and actual scale R=4-sum f_i^2 from Sections 2--3 are available.
The barycentric argument in Section 6 of
`candidate 919c51f1d263878e`
gives source coordinates alpha_i<5/14 and q_i>20/49.

We also need a lower bound on their sum. Write
eta_i=5/14-alpha_i>0. Then sum eta_i=1/14 and

    sum alpha_i^2=65/196+sum eta_i^2<66/196=33/98.

Consequently sum q_i>=4sum_(i<j)alpha_i alpha_j>65/49.
On the other hand the actual overlap surplus satisfies

    0<=E/k=3r-sum q_i-alpha
       <=4/3+alpha/3-sum q_i
       <125/93-sum q_i=Delta.

Thus the full geometric common-budget data imply

    0<Delta<80/4557.                                     (11)

In particular the symmetric cap-sum constraint of the ordinary scalar
closure is automatic here; it has not been imposed on K separately.

Fix an index i with present R_i. Since delta_i=(a-U_j-U_k)_+,

    U_i-sqrt(U_i delta_i)<=E.

If delta_i>0 this follows from sqrt(U_i delta_i)>=delta_i and
U_i-delta_i=E; if delta_i=0 then a<=U_j+U_k and U_i<=E.
Lemma 1 and the exact scale estimate therefore give, writing

    N_i=f_i/sqrt(q_i),      L=sqrt(beta R),
    t_i=sigma_Ai/sigma_Ki,

the bound

    t_i<=N_i Delta/L.                                    (12)

Here L>sqrt((30/31)(201/400))>697/1000 by (3), (10), and
the positive square gap 14921/31000000.

Suppose for a contradiction that p_i<=2/9. Relabel i=1 and put

    x=f_1, t=sqrt(q_1), g=f_2+f_3, F=x+g,
    m=sqrt(20/49), s=sqrt(c), rho=sqrt(119/279),
    N=x/t, Z=f_2/sqrt(q_2)+f_3/sqrt(q_3).

As in the ordinary scalar proof, the three Lorentz inequalities give
F<=3, while the moment gives F>=2/s>59/20. The exact mixed weights,
with every other endpoint ratio nonnegative, satisfy

    p_1>=N/[N+(1+2t_1)Z]
        >=xm/[3s(1+2x Delta/(mL))].                       (13)

Using p_1<=2/9 in (13) yields

    x<=[2s/(3m)]/[1-4s Delta/(3m^2 L)]<3/4.              (14)

The denominator is positive. A fully rational certificate for its
positivity and the final comparison uses

    s<33867/50000, m>63887/100000,
    m^2=20/49, L>697/1000, Delta<80/4557.

The resulting upper bound in (14) is

    24392142300/32586905977
        =3/4-192148731/130347623908<3/4.

We repeat the constrained square-root tangent argument while keeping
its slack. Both other f_j must exceed (s/rho)x. Otherwise, since
s/rho<26/25, T=x+f_j<153/100; the remaining Lorentz inequality gives

    F<=2+T-T^2/4<117791/40000<59/20,

contrary to the moment lower bound. The square-root tangents at
(119/279,c,c), with sum q_i=125/93-Delta, now give

    2<=rho x+s g-x Delta/(2rho)
       <=rho x+2s sqrt(2-x)-x Delta/(2rho).               (15)

Explicitly, after the three tangent inequalities are added, their
linear remainder is

    -x Delta/(2rho)
      +sum_(j=2,3)[f_j/(2s)-x/(2rho)](q_j-c).

The two coefficients in brackets are positive, and q_j-c<=0, which
proves the first bound in (15) with the retained slack.

Put B(x)=rho x+2s sqrt(2-x)-2. As before B(67/100)<0, with the
exact rational upper-bound gap 10269/78125000. The function rho x+
2s sqrt(2-x) is increasing for 0<x<=3/4: its derivative is positive
because (5/4)(119/279)-128/279=83/1116>0. Thus (15) implies

    67/100<x<3/4,
    Delta<=2rho B(x)/x.                                  (16)

On this interval B'(x)<1/10. Indeed rho<2/3, s>2/3, and
sqrt(2-x)<7/6 give B'(x)<2/21<1/10. If z=x-67/100>0, then

    B(x)<z/10.

Also 4rho/(mL)<6. The rational bounds already used give the upper
ratio 261236000/44529239<6. Combining (12) and (16) gives

    1+2t_1 <=1+2x Delta/(mL)<1+3z/5.                     (17)

Use the reciprocal secant (20) from the ordinary scalar proof. The
moment identity and t<=s give

    Z/N <= zeta(x)
      :=[2(m+s)sqrt(2-x)-2+xs]/(mx).                    (18)

Indeed first Z/N<=t[2(m+s)sqrt(2-x)-2+xt]/(msx).
The quantity 2(m+s)sqrt(2-x)-2 is positive on this interval, since
m+s>13/10 and sqrt(2-x)>1. Thus replacing each occurrence of t by s
in that upper bound preserves its direction and proves (18).

The exact ordinary certificate G(67/100)>0 shows
zeta(67/100)<7/2. On the interval in (16),

    zeta'(x)
      =[2-(m+s)(4-x)/sqrt(2-x)]/(m x^2)<-4.              (19)

For explicit elementary bounds, m+s>13/10,
(4-x)/sqrt(2-x)>=2sqrt(2)>14/5, and
m x^2<(2/3)(3/4)^2=3/8. The resulting derivative bound is
-328/75<-4. Therefore zeta(x)<7/2-4z. The right side is positive
on 0<z<2/25; so (17)--(19) give

    (1+2t_1)Z/N
       <(1+3z/5)(7/2-4z)
       =7/2-(19/10)z-(12/5)z^2<7/2.

Equation (13)'s first bound now gives p_1>2/9, a contradiction.
All section estimates used (12) only for the chosen present corner;
no assumption on absent corners was introduced. QED.

## 6. A scoped contraction consequence with strict endpoint gaps

Retain Theorem 3's hypotheses. Suppose additionally that the three
displayed caps genuinely attain depth Q at (0,y), and that Q is the
global maximum unnormalized depth on

    S=({-1} times A) union ({0} times K) union ({1} times B).

Assume the maximum raw depth restricted to each endpoint fiber is
strictly smaller than Q. Then this configuration is not a local
minimum of the normalized maximum depth under admissible convex-body
variations of the three fibers.

Here is the full local descent argument. Genuine criticality and
actual midpoint inclusion give the audited chord-gauge bound
max p_i<=3/4 from
`candidate 86934b651b11f7d5`.
Thus every pair of capture weights has sum at least 1/4. Almost every
point of A is captured by at least one of its three halfplanes. If it
is captured by exactly one, that index has a present residual corner,
so its weight is greater than 2/9 by Theorem 3. If it is captured by
two or three caps, its weight sum is at least 1/4 or 1. There are only
finitely many signatures. Consequently there is a constant tau>2/9
such that

    sum_i p_i 1_(H_i^A)(x)>=tau       for almost every x in A.       (20)

Fix any contraction center p in A and set A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p). These
bodies are nested in A. Integrating (20) on the actual removed shell
gives

    sum_i p_i[U_i-|A_t intersect H_i^A|]
       >=tau[a-|A_t|].

The proper sections are continuous as their thresholds vary. Thus
the cap derivatives at t=0 exist, and, writing L_i for the removed
cap derivative, one obtains

    sum_i p_i L_i>=2tau a>4a/9.                           (21)

For completeness, reoptimize the meeting point of the three fixed-normal
caps. For a nearby point y' and small t define

    G_i(y',t)=|A_t intersect {v_i.x>=2v_i.y'-h_B(v_i)}|
                 +|K intersect {v_i.x>=v_i.y'}|.

Properness makes these functions continuously differentiable near
(y,0). Their y' derivatives are -(2sigma_Ai+sigma_Ki)v_i. The three
equations G_i(y_t,t)=Q_t have an invertible Jacobian in the two
coordinates of y_t and the scalar Q_t: a vector in its kernel would
satisfy v_i.z=-u/(2sigma_Ai+sigma_Ki); summing over i gives u=0 and
then z=0. The implicit function theorem supplies y_t in int K and Q_t.
Multiplying the differentiated equations by p_i and using the balanced
normals gives

    Q'_0=-sum_i p_i L_i.

Every point of the middle fiber belongs to at least one of the three
new caps, because their continuous normals sum to zero. Its raw depth
is therefore at most Q_t. The contracted set S_t is contained in S;
raw depths at its endpoint points cannot exceed their old raw depths.
The strict endpoint gaps consequently keep all endpoint depths below
Q_t for sufficiently small t. Hence the new global maximum raw depth
is at most Q_t.

The total area is M_t=a(1-t)^2+k+b, so M'_0=-2a. Equations (9) and
(21) give

    (Q_t/M_t)'_(t=0)
       =[-M sum_i p_i L_i+2aQ]/M^2<0.

Finally, the convex hull of the three lifted fibers A_t,K,B is a full
three-dimensional convex body whose integer fibers are exactly those
three: its possible extra midpoint contribution (A_t+B)/2 lies in K.
Thus this is an actual admissible variation, not an independently
assigned cap perturbation.

This excludes a local extremizer only in the stated triangular-middle,
small-A, proper-critical, nonheavy-B, strict-endpoint-gap branch. It
does not establish that a global minimizer exists, does not handle
tied endpoint depths, and does not prove the result for a general
middle body or arbitrary n,d.
